concerns.location: plan.md: Summary item (3) and Phase 3; quickstart.md 'Current data status'
concerns.text: The plan claims the 'Cycle-Agnostic fallback (GSN-only RF)' will 'produce the reconstruction' when TSI is absent. But the fallback is a supervised GSN→TSI regressor — with NO verified TSI target of any kind, it cannot be trained either. FR-003 forbids using CMIP6 for training. As written, the 1610–2002 reconstruction (Phase 5, FR-004) would be produced by an untrained or fabricated model, making the primary deliverable (and SC-003 variance comparisons on it) scientifically meaningless. The plan must either (a) make the reconstruction itself conditional/skipped when no TSI target exists, or (b) obtain a verified TSI target — not assert a fallback that has no training signal.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 4 / FR-009, SC-005; data-model.md SensitivityResult
concerns.text: FR-009 defines the sensitivity sweep over 'cycle-specific calibration coefficients'. With training skipped, no calibration coefficients exist; the plan vaguely substitutes 'reconstruction sensitivity' and SensitivityResult.rmse_variation is nullable. The sweep as planned has no well-defined estimand in the no-TSI path — specify what quantity is actually swept and how it is computed without a trained model, or make Phase 4 conditional too.

concerns.location: plan.md: Constitution Check Principle VI; research.md §2.3
concerns.text: Constitution Principle VI mandates validation on held-out satellite-era data (2016–present) with training 2003–2015. The plan substitutes leave-one-cycle-out CV 'conditional on TSI availability' and documents the spec-vs-constitution cycle-detection deviation, but never addresses the mandated train/validation split. State explicitly how Principle VI's validation requirement is satisfied or formally deferred given TSI unavailability.

concerns.location: spec.md:FR-014, FR-013, SC-001
concerns.text: FR-014 ('MUST ingest a verified SORCE/TIM satellite TSI dataset... sole training target') and FR-013/SC-001 (2007 baseline, rmse_reduction_percentage) are MUST-level requirements with NO backing plan element — Phase 3 is explicitly conditional and skipped today. The plan flags this honestly, but the spec remains contradictory: it mandates data that no verified source provides. Spec must be revised (make TSI/baseline conditional or re-source) before the plan can claim full coverage.

concerns.location: spec.md:FR-002 vs plan.md Phase 2 / Data Availability
concerns.text: FR-002 defines the low-activity proxy as 'a fixed value representing the average total solar irradiance observed during the 2008–2019 minimum, expressed in W/m²'. The plan instead fills gaps with 'mean GSN over the 2008–2019 minimum' — a sunspot-number unit, not a W/m² TSI value. This is a spec/plan mismatch on a MUST requirement; either the spec's proxy definition or the plan's implementation must be reconciled.

concerns.location: spec.md:SC-002 vs plan.md Phase 3
concerns.text: SC-002 (R² against observed satellite TSI) is only 'conditional' in the plan; as written the spec makes it a measurable outcome with no fallback measurement. Same root cause as FR-014, but the spec should state the degraded-path success criterion explicitly rather than the plan silently nulling it.

concerns.location: constitution.md Principle VI vs plan.md Phase 3
concerns.text: Constitution VI mandates validation on held-out satellite-era data 2016–present (training 2003–2015). The plan uses leave-one-cycle-out CV only and never mentions the 2016–present holdout split. The plan documents the Principle VII Hilbert-Huang deviation but is silent on this Principle VI validation-split requirement — an unbacked constitutional MUST.

concerns.location: spec.md Edge case 3 vs plan.md Phase 2
concerns.text: Spec edge case requires a documented calibration/gap-filling correction for SORCE/TIM instrument drift with sensitivity analysis on the correction method. The plan's conditional TSI path mentions only 'attempted; flagged unavailable' and no drift-correction step even for the future TSI-available branch. Add it to the conditional Phase 1/3 path or note the spec gap.

concerns.location: research.md:1 Dataset Strategy table, GSN row
concerns.text: The 'verified' GSN URL is https://huggingface.co/datasets/Francesco/construction-safety-gsnvb/... — the repository name indicates a construction-safety dataset, not a Group Sunspot Number series. The plan itself demonstrates that other URLs in the same verified block were content mismatches (Ethereum/chat/Amazon). The plan asserts 'monthly historical sunspot record — satisfies FR-001' without evidence the file contains date + sunspot variables. If this is a wrong-dataset, the primary predictor for the entire project is invalid; the plan must verify the actual columns/content of this parquet before building on it, or the GSN source is a dataset-variable-fit failure.

concerns.location: research.md:1 Dataset Strategy table, CMIP6 row
concerns.text: The CMIP6 source is a 'wip_cmip6' test shard (test-00000-of-00012.parquet) with key variables listed as 'time, solar forcing / TSI variable' — the slash suggests uncertainty about whether a TSI/solar-forcing variable actually exists in this shard. FR-010/FR-011 depend on a CMIP6 v3.2 solar-forcing TSI series; the plan should confirm the shard contains that variable (and at what temporal resolution/coverage, e.g. whether it spans 1610–present for the minima comparisons) rather than assuming it.

concerns.location: plan.md:Summary item (3) and Phase 3/5; research.md §2.1 'Cycle-Agnostic fallback'
concerns.text: With no verified TSI dataset, the Cycle-Agnostic fallback (GSN-only RF/GP mapping GSN→TSI) also has NO training target — a GSN-only feature set still requires TSI labels to fit any regressor. Yet Phase 5 states the fallback 'produces the reconstruction' with 95% prediction intervals. As written, the reconstruction output (FR-004, tsi_reconstruction_1610_2002.parquet) is infeasible: there is no data resource from which any GSN→TSI mapping can be learned. The plan must either identify a verified TSI training source or state that FR-004/FR-005/SC-003 outputs cannot be produced at all (not merely 'degraded'), and flag this at the spec level.

concerns.location: contracts/dataset.schema.yaml vs contracts/dataset_schema.schema.yaml vs contracts/dataset_schema.yaml
concerns.text: Three overlapping, mutually contradictory dataset schemas exist. dataset_schema.schema.yaml REQUIRES cycle_phase_sin/cycle_phase_cos and omits cycle_id; the plan/data-model use one-hot cycle_id + gsn_lag1 and never mention cycle phase features. Phase 7's test_contracts.py 'validates outputs against contracts/*.schema.yaml' — against WHICH one? Pick one canonical schema (SSoT, Principle I) and delete/merge the others.

concerns.location: contracts/output.schema.yaml vs contracts/output_schema.schema.yaml vs contracts/reconstruction.schema.yaml
concerns.text: Three overlapping output schemas with conflicting field names (tsi_lower vs tsi_uncertainty_lower) and conflicting required metrics. output.schema.yaml requires rmse_train/rmse_validation/r2_train/r2_validation as non-nullable 'number', which contradicts the documented skip path (training skipped when TSI absent → metrics null per report.schema.yaml). Designate one SSoT output schema and make metric types nullable-or-conditional.

concerns.location: plan.md Constitution Check, Principle VI row
concerns.text: Constitution VI mandates validation 'on held-out satellite-era data (2016–present)' with training 2003–2015; the plan uses leave-one-cycle-out CV instead and marks VI ✅ without acknowledging this deviation. The VII row documents its Hilbert-Huang deviation; VI needs the same explicit treatment (or the plan must add the 2016+ holdout).

concerns.location: plan.md Phase 2 / Data Availability vs spec.md FR-002
concerns.text: FR-002 defines the ≥1yr low-activity proxy as 'a fixed value representing the average total solar irradiance observed during the 2008–2019 minimum, expressed in W/m²'; the plan/research use 'mean GSN over the 2008–2019 minimum' — a dimensionless sunspot number, not W/m². Cross-doc disagreement on the proxy's units/definition; reconcile or document the deviation.

concerns.location: plan.md Phase 2 / research.md §2.2 vs data-model.md SunspotRecord
concerns.text: The 'facular baseline offset term' is listed as an engineered feature in the plan and research, but no data-model entity or contract schema defines a field for it. Either add it to SunspotRecord/preprocessed schema or state it is a model-internal constant not persisted in data.

concerns.location: plan.md Project Structure vs data-model.md Storage Layout
concerns.text: data-model lists data/raw/checksums.json and data/artifacts/figures/reconstruction.png; the plan's project-structure tree omits checksums.json (only mentioned in prose) — minor, but the trees should agree since T005/T006 verifier rejections show contract/schema artifacts are being tracked literally.

concerns.location: plan.md: Summary item (3)/(5); Phase 3 & Phase 5; quickstart.md 'Current data status'
concerns.text: With TSI unavailable, training is 'skipped', yet the 'Cycle-Agnostic fallback (GSN-only RF)' still 'produces the reconstruction' (Phase 5, quickstart). A regressor needs a target; with no TSI training target the fallback model is undefined. Either it is trained on CMIP6 solar forcing — which violates FR-003 ('CMIP6 is NOT used for model training') and makes the Phase-6 CMIP6 comparison circular (validating the reconstruction against its own training target) — or it cannot exist. The plan must state explicitly what, if anything, the fallback is fit against, and if nothing, the 1610–2002 'reconstruction' is not a scientific output and Phase 5/6 as planned cannot run.

concerns.location: plan.md Phase 6 / FR-005 / SC-003; research.md §3 gap handling
concerns.text: SC-003 variance comparison across Maunder/Dalton/Modern minima is tautological under the planned gap handling: Maunder-Minimum-scale gaps (≥1 yr) are filled with a CONSTANT low-activity proxy, so the reconstructed TSI variance in the Maunder minimum is near-zero BY CONSTRUCTION, not empirically. The bootstrap test of variance differences across minima would 'confirm' a difference that is an artifact of the imputation rule. The plan needs either proxy values with realistic variability or an explicit statement that Maunder-minimum variance is not interpretable.

concerns.location: plan.md Phase 2 / FR-002; research.md §3
concerns.text: FR-002 defines the low-activity proxy as 'average total solar irradiance observed during the 2008–2019 minimum, expressed in W/m²', but the plan/research substitute 'mean GSN over the 2008–2019 minimum' — a sunspot number, not an irradiance. This is a unit/category error in the imputation and changes what the proxy means downstream.

The plan does not state what quantity the {0.01, 0.05, 0.1} threshold sweep operates on in the degraded path; as written Phase 4 has no well-defined object of analysis.

new_concerns.text: FR‑001 requires ingestion of both GSN and a verified SORCE/TIM TSI dataset. The plan attempts to ingest TSI only conditionally and skips it entirely when no verified source is found, leaving the requirement unfulfilled.

FR‑003 calls for training a Cycle‑Agnostic fallback model (GSN‑only) to handle pre‑satellite cycles. The plan only trains this fallback when a primary TSI model is trained; if TSI is unavailable, the fallback is never instantiated, violating the requirement.

FR‑004 mandates generation of a pre‑satellite TSI reconstruction (1610–2002) with uncertainty bands. The plan omits this step entirely when TSI data are missing, resulting in a missing required artifact.

FR‑005 requires a statistical comparison of reconstructed TSI variance across Maunder, Dalton, and Modern minima using 1000‑iteration bootstrap. The plan’s variance comparison is conditional on having a reconstruction; without TSI data the analysis is skipped, leaving the requirement unmet.
FR‑013 (ingest the 2007 baseline reconstruction) is a MUST requirement, yet the plan flags the baseline as unavailable and proceeds without it, violating the specification.
SC‑001 (≥15 % RMSE reduction versus the 2007 baseline) cannot be evaluated because the baseline dataset is missing and the plan reports the metric as null. The success criterion remains unaddressed.
SC‑003 (bootstrap variance comparison across solar minima) depends on having a reconstruction. Since the reconstruction is omitted when TSI is unavailable, this success criterion cannot be measured.

SC‑005 (sensitivity analysis over inconsistency‑tolerance thresholds) is performed only if a model is trained. With TSI unavailable, the analysis is skipped, leaving the required sensitivity assessment unfulfilled.

new_concerns.location: Constitution Check table – Principle VII row
new_concerns.text: Constitution Principle VII mandates cycle‑boundary detection via Hilbert‑Huang transform, yet the plan describes using the SILSO‑method 13‑month smoothed peak detection. The Constitution Check marks the principle as ✅ without reconciling this mismatch. Update the plan to employ Hilbert‑Huang detection (or amend the constitution) and reflect the change in the check table.

new_concerns.location: plan.md Phase 6 / FR-005 / SC-003; research.md §3 gap handling
new_concerns.text: Variance comparison across Maunder, Dalton, and Modern minima remains tautological because gaps ≥1 yr are filled with a fixed low‑activity TSI proxy (1360.8 W/m²). This forces near‑zero variance in the Maunder Minimum, so the bootstrap variance test will simply confirm a difference that is an artifact of the imputation rule. Adding a disclaimer does not resolve the methodological flaw; the plan must either (a) replace the constant proxy with a stochastic proxy that reflects realistic variability, or (b) exclude the Maunder Minimum from the variance analysis and clearly state the limitation.

Phase 7's test_contracts.py 'validates outputs against contracts/*.schema.yaml' — against WHICH one? Pick one canonical schema (SSoT, Principle I) and delete/merge the others.

concerns.location: contracts/output.schema.yaml vs contracts/output_schema.schema.yaml vs contracts/reconstruction.schema.yaml
concerns.text: Three overlapping output schemas with conflicting field names (tsi_lower vs tsi_uncertainty_lower) and conflicting required metrics. output.schema.yaml requires rmse_train/rmse_validation/r2_train/r2_validation as non-nullable 'number', which contradicts the documented skip path (training skipped when TSI absent → metrics null per report.schema.yaml). Designate one SSoT output schema and make metric types nullable-or-conditional.
